expected_level_description: You can: - apply your clinical knowledge to digital work within your scope of practice - keep your registration and continuing professional development up to date - give clinical opinions on workflows, content, and safety
You can: - give clinical input to product teams on workflows and safety - help clinical colleagues adopt new systems
You can: - map current and future clinical workflows with clinicians and care staff - test system configuration against clinical scenarios - write clear clinical requirements for product teams
You can: - take part in hazard workshops and contribute to a hazard log - follow the clinical risk management process for your work - provide evidence for a clinical safety case, such as test results
You can: - find and use the right codes for a data item or form - use terminology browsers and reference sets

skill: Human factors and usability in clinical systems
expected_level_description: You can: - take part in usability tests and simulations of clinical tasks - spot common design hazards, such as similar-looking options or hidden alerts
You can: - apply data protection principles to your work - contribute to data protection impact assessments - handle information requests and records correctly

You can: - listen to the needs of design and business stakeholders and interpret information - take part in discussions within a multidisciplinary team - be an advocate for the team externally, and can manage differing perspectives - shape and share communications relevant to the audience

You can: - identify and engage with users or stakeholders to collate user needs evidence - understand and define research that fits user needs - use quantitative and qualitative data about users to turn user focus into outcomes
